overview: This Senate resolution names June 2026 "Great Outdoors Month." It points to government figures showing outdoor recreation, such as hiking, camping, fishing and boating, is a large part of the U.S. economy, and notes past laws that pay for upkeep of public lands and waters. It also says many outdoor recreation businesses are small businesses important to rural towns. The resolution encourages everyone in the country to enjoy the outdoors responsibly in June and all year. It does not create any program or spend any money. As of July 14, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say it highlights how outdoor recreation supports jobs, health and rural economies, and encourages people to use and value public lands.
against: Critics say it is symbolic, was approved after the month had already ended, and does not change any law or spending.
